# Psalm 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. For the-flutes. A-psalm of-David.

**2** Give-ear-to my-words, YHWH; consider my-groaning.

**3** Attend to-the-sound of-my-cry, my-King and-my-God, for to-You I-pray.

**4** YHWH, in-the-morning You-hear my-voice; in-the-morning I-set-in-order [my prayer] to-You and-I-watch.

**5** For not a-God delighting-in wickedness [are] You; evil does-not sojourn with-You.

**6** The-boastful shall-not stand before Your-eyes; You-hate all workers-of iniquity.

**7** You-destroy speakers-of falsehood; a-man of-blood and-deceit YHWH abhors.

**8** But-I, in-the-abundance of-Your-steadfast-love, I-enter Your-house; I-bow-down toward Your-holy temple in-Your-fear.

**9** YHWH, lead-me in-Your-righteousness because-of my-enemies; make-straight before-me Your-way.

**10** For there-is-no faithfulness in-their-mouth; their-inward-part [is] destruction; an-open tomb [is] their-throat; their-tongue they-make-smooth.

**11** Hold-them-guilty, O-God; let-them-fall by-their-own counsels; in-the-multitude of-their-transgressions drive-them-out, for they-have-rebelled against-You.

**12** But-let-rejoice all who-take-refuge in-You; forever let-them-sing-for-joy. And-You-shelter over-them, and-let-exult in-You those-who-love Your-name.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **5:4**: Set-in-order (arokh) is a sacrificial term — arranging offerings on the altar. Morning prayer is presented as a morning sacrifice.

- **5:10**: 'Open tomb' — their speech is deathly, consuming those who hear it. Paul quotes this in Romans 3:13.

— EMET
